title: OA WEAPONS PROSE - the forty-seven weapon descriptions
audit_comment: OA round one hundred fifty-nine (capture pp. 84-93): the weapons prose - the forty-seven weapon descriptions pinned as the essence-of-the-weapon doctrines, the tool-and-weapon duality, the ninja concealment thread, and the mechanics consts of the chu-ko-nu magazine, the needle burst die, the lasso pulls, the man catcher, the metsubishi, the nekode climb bonus, the shuriken star points, and the tetsu-bishi area rules (the descriptions re-captured at pp. 42-51 of the compressed-3 re-upload)

consts.name: dnjChuKoNuMagazineQuarrels
consts.comment: the chu-ko-nu magazine capacity - up to 10 quarrels held in the top magazine (print capture pp. 84-93)

consts.name: dnjChuKoNuReloadPerRound
consts.comment: the chu-ko-nu reload rate - up to two quarrels reloaded into the magazine per round (print capture pp. 84-93)

consts.name: dnjChuKoNuFullReloadRounds
consts.comment: the chu-ko-nu full reload - five rounds required to completely reload the magazine (print capture pp. 84-93)

consts.name: dnjNeedleMouthCarryMax
consts.comment: the needle mouth-carry maximum - up to 20 needles carried in the mouth (print capture pp. 84-93)

consts.name: dnjNeedleAllFiredDieSides
consts.comment: the needle all-fired die - when all 20 are fired at once, 1d20 rolled for the damage (print capture pp. 84-93)

consts.name: dnjShurikenStarPointMinimum
consts.comment: the shuriken star point minimum - the stars have three or more razor-edged points so at least one strikes (print capture pp. 84-93)

consts.name: dnjNekodeClimbBonusPercent
consts.comment: the nekode climb bonus - the climbing chance increased by 5 percent when the spikes are jammed into cracks (print capture pp. 84-93)

consts.name: dnjLassoLineCuttingDamage
consts.comment: the lasso line durability - the line can take 2 points of cutting damage (print capture pp. 84-93)

consts.name: dnjLassoBipedalPullPercent
consts.comment: the lasso pull chance - the bipedal creature on foot and no more than half the wielder's weight pulled off its feet 25 percent of the time (print capture pp. 84-93)

consts.name: dnjLassoExtraPullerBonusPercent
consts.comment: the lasso extra-puller bonus - roughly 20 percent per additional creature pulling on the rope (print capture pp. 84-93)

consts.name: dnjManCatcherOffFeetPercent
consts.comment: the man catcher pull chance - the 25 percent chance the caught victim is pulled off his feet to a kneeling or prone position (print capture pp. 84-93)

consts.name: dnjManCatcherHaftCuttingDamage
consts.comment: the man catcher haft durability - 6 points of cutting damage required to chop through the haft for a rescue (print capture pp. 84-93)

consts.name: dnjMetsubishiIncapacitationMaxRounds
consts.comment: the metsubishi incapacitation - the failed save incapacitating for 1-6 rounds, the maximum six (print capture pp. 84-93)

consts.name: dnjTetsubishiBaseCount
consts.comment: the tetsu-bishi base count - the base amount of 10 cast down in the area (print capture pp. 84-93)

consts.name: dnjTetsubishiBaseAreaSquareFeet
consts.comment: the tetsu-bishi base area - the 5 by 5 foot area, 25 square feet covered by the base count (print capture pp. 84-93)

consts.name: dnjTetsubishiHalfCountSavePenalty
consts.comment: the tetsu-bishi halved-count penalty - the victim gains a -4 on the saving throw when half the base amount is used (print capture pp. 84-93)

consts.name: dnjTetsubishiPerFiveExtraSavePenalty
consts.comment: the tetsu-bishi per-five penalty - for every 5 above the base count the saving throw is reduced by 2 (print capture pp. 84-93)

consts.name: dnjTetsubishiStepDamageMax
consts.comment: the tetsu-bishi step damage - the stepped-on victim suffering 1-4 points of damage, the maximum four (print capture pp. 84-93)

consts.name: dnjTetsubishiLameDurationHours
consts.comment: the tetsu-bishi lame watch - the failed second save leaving the victim at one-third movement for 24 hours or until healed (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjArrowsDoctrine
bools.comment: the five arrow types - the wedge head, the narrow spike-head armor piercer, the v frog crotch cutting standards and cords, the whistling humming bulb signal arrow doubling as the 1-3 damage fire arrow, and the broad leaf head with its carved artistic designs (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjBoStickDoctrine
bools.comment: the bo stick - the 6 to 7 foot hard-wood staff, difficult to cut or break (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjBokuTohDoctrine
bools.comment: the boku-toh - the wooden katana copy for practice, still able to injure from the force of the blow (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjChainDoctrine
bools.comment: the chain - the manriki-gusari or rante, a weighted length of chain for whirling blows, entangling, or bola-like throwing, worn as a belt or under a sash and favored by ninjas (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjChijirikiDoctrine
bools.comment: the chijiriki - the spear with a weighted chain on the butt end, used as a spear or swung to entangle (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjChopsticksDoctrine
bools.comment: the chopsticks - an emergency weapon, not very effective but better than nothing (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjChuKoNuDoctrine
bools.comment: the chu-ko-nu - the repeating light crossbow with its 10-quarrel magazine worked by a single lever, faster fire but heavier and poorer range, and no firing and reloading in the same round (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjDaikyuDoctrine
bools.comment: the daikyu - the largest bow, seven feet and bent at the ends, the off-center grip allowing fire from horseback and kneeling (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjFangDoctrine
bools.comment: the fang - the heavy iron elephant-goad weapon of short-sword length, the sharp point with the heavy hooked point below (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjGunsenDoctrine
bools.comment: the gunsen - the iron war fan, defensive as a small shield and normally a weapon of emergency (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjJitteDoctrine
bools.comment: the jitte - the defensive tapered iron bar with the short hook near the handle, blocking attacks and catching weapons (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjJoStickDoctrine
bools.comment: the jo stick - the one-hand smaller bo stick of the same wood, often used in pairs (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjKamaDoctrine
bools.comment: the kama - the straight-bladed farmer's sickle carried without suspicion and used to great effect by ninjas (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjKatanaDoctrine
bools.comment: the katana - the single-edged slightly curved chisel-point sword of superior construction, the weapon-smith's rare art, light and well-balanced, razor-sharp, often decorated and often carrying individual names of glory (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjKatanaHonorDoctrine
bools.comment: the katana honor doctrine - the sword as the samurai's personal weapon and family honor, the touch of the scabbard and the unpermitted draw as insults, the generational heirloom, the loss a disgrace swept clean only by recovery and punishment, and the price varying with workmanship and history (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjKauSinKeDoctrine
bools.comment: the kau sin ke - the whipping chain of four to six short iron bars joined by chain links, the agricultural-flail origin, the bars wrapping around shields to land crushing blows (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjKawanagaDoctrine
bools.comment: the kawanaga - the rope with the grappling hook at one end and the weight at the other, a climbing tool doubling as a swinging or entangling weapon popular with ninjas (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjKiseruDoctrine
bools.comment: the kiseru - the metal tobacco pipe whose innocent look hides its clubbing use, cheap and popular with peasants and monks (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjKumadeDoctrine
bools.comment: the kumade - the rake-headed climbing pole doubling as a weapon, a common ninja item for its innocent uses (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjKusariGamaDoctrine
bools.comment: the kusari-gama - the sickle developed for fighting with the weighted chain on the handle butt, attacking with the kama, clubbing and entangling with the chain, or whirling the kama at the chain's end, easy to make and favored by peasants and ninjas (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjKyoketsuogiDoctrine
bools.comment: the kyoketsuogi - the rope with the sharp hooked blade at one end and the heavy iron ring at the other, swung, snapped to entangle, thrown like a bola, or held while striking with the knife, nearly silent and easily concealed (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjLajatangDoctrine
bools.comment: the lajatang - the rare three-to-five-foot shaft with a crescent blade at each end, some with downward barbs, wielded two-handed like a staff by the skilled martial artist (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjLassoDoctrine
bools.comment: the lasso - the no-damage entangling weapon, the saving throw versus poison to cut free, the automatic dismount without horsemanship, the pull-off-feet chance for lighter bipedal creatures, the combined pullers, and the bend bars attempt against the line (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjManCatcherDoctrine
bools.comment: the man catcher - the two-pronged pole arm encircling man-sized creatures, the size limits, the spikes and sharpened edges, the lost shield and dexterity bonuses, the push and pull damage, the bend bars escape, and the rescue by chopping the haft (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjMetsubishiDoctrine
bools.comment: the metsubishi - the wooden powder blower with its mouthpiece, chamber, and tube, doing no damage but incapacitating on a failed save, used by ninjas and city constables (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjNagimakiDoctrine
bools.comment: the nagimaki - the shortened naginata used by horsemen (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjNaginataDoctrine
bools.comment: the naginata - the lightweight but strong six-to-eight-foot glaive ending in the curved sword-like blade, the standard polearm often preferred by women (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjNeedleDoctrine
bools.comment: the needle - the mouth-carried needles fired by spitting or blowing, singly or in bursts, of poor range and almost never effective against armor, a dishonorable weapon of surprise and distraction (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjNekodeDoctrine
bools.comment: the nekode - the climbing spikes worn on straps or gloves, also clawing an opponent for small damage while leaving the hands free (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjNinjaToDoctrine
bools.comment: the ninja-to - the ninja's straight lower-quality short sword with the multi-use scabbard, the secret compartments, the open-ended blowpipe or breathing tube, the climbing silk cord, and the DM-allowed hidden devices (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjNunchakuDoctrine
bools.comment: the nunchaku - the two-handed martial-arts flail of two lengths joined by chain or cord, parrying, clubbing, and catching weapons, easily concealed (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjParangDoctrine
bools.comment: the parang - the tribesman's heavy-bladed machete of chopping force, a tool and weapon in one (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjPelletBowDoctrine
bools.comment: the pellet bow - the bow with the small sling in the bowstring holding a stone or clay or lead pellet, fired with more force than a sling (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjSaiDoctrine
bools.comment: the sai or tjabang - the martial-arts jitte almost identical in use, the two projecting prongs instead of one (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjSangKauwDoctrine
bools.comment: the sang kauw - the double-headed spear with the loop handle and its dagger or crescent projection, one-hand parry and attack, the second buckler form counting as a small shield, and the great training required (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjShakenDoctrine
bools.comment: the shaken - the shuriken-like throwing weapon used in the same way (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjShakujoYariDoctrine
bools.comment: the shakujo yari - the spear sheathed to look like a staff, used as a bo stick when sheathed and carried to look defenseless (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjShikomiZueDoctrine
bools.comment: the shikomi-zue - the staff concealing the spring spear head, doing bo stick or spear damage, and hiding other weapons inside (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjShurikenDoctrine
bools.comment: the shuriken - the small throwing weapon of stars with three or more razor-edged points in large and small sizes and the tapering spike pins, easily concealed in clothing, sashes, or hair (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjSiangkamDoctrine
bools.comment: the siangkam - the metal-shafted arrow with the wooden handle, used in pairs to jab, thrust, slash, and parry, and never thrown effectively, needing the trained martial-arts style (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjSodeGaramiDoctrine
bools.comment: the sode garami - the sleeve entangler, the pole and crossbar of spikes and hooks catching clothing without harm, the saving throw versus paralyzation to escape, and the constables' and palace guards' carry (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjTetsubishiDoctrine
bools.comment: the tetsu-bishi - the caltrops of the four-sided spiked diamond cast on the ground to stop pursuit, the area rules with the base count and the saving throw versus paralyzation, the halved-count and per-five penalties, the fast-movement and cautious-move rules, and the lamed-aftermath watch (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjTetsuboDoctrine
bools.comment: the tetsubo - the iron-shod rod, the polearm mace of the long wooden rod wielded with two hands, doubling as a traveler's walking stick (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjThreePieceRodDoctrine
bools.comment: the three-piece rod - the martial-arts flail of three two-to-three-foot pieces of hard wood joined by short chains, striking, blocking, and catching or breaking weapons in trained hands and useless otherwise (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjTuiFaDoctrine
bools.comment: the tui-fa or tonfa - the hardwood rod with the off-center millstone-handle grip, blocking, catching, breaking, and attacking in trained hands, used where normal weapons are barred (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjUchiNeDoctrine
bools.comment: the uchi-ne - the short heavy javelin looking like a miniature arrow, thrown short distances or used for thrusting, often carried by traveling nobles (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjWakizashiDoctrine
bools.comment: the wakizashi - the short sword matching the katana in design and naming, the daisho long-and-short pair worn only by samurai under penalty of arrest or execution, with the katana rules applying to the matched set (print capture pp. 84-93)

bools.name: dnjWhipDoctrine
bools.comment: the whip - the weapon needing exposed or lightly covered flesh, the heavy clothing and thick hide protections, and the entangle use often more effective than the damage (print capture pp. 84-93)

examples.note: the chu-ko-nu reload math - five rounds at two per round fills the ten-quarrel magazine
the needle burst die - all twenty fired at once roll the twenty-sided die
the lasso pull math - the base chance minus the extra-puller bonus is five
the pull chances agree - the lasso and the man catcher both pull at twenty-five
the tetsu-bishi save math - the halved-count penalty plus the per-five penalty is six
the tetsu-bishi lame watch - twenty-four hours is six times the step damage maximum
